scope: R204: complete feasible solution for the encoder under-2s target - load to device once and release the host copy

refutes_r203_solution_2.proposal: exclude the vision tower from pinning since text-only prompts do not need it
refutes_r203_solution_2.verdict: vision is only 0.82 GB against a 30.7 GB shortfall, so it closes 2.7 percent and the proposal is withdrawn
refutes_r203_solution_2.model_reconciliation: text plus vision is 64.8 GB against a 63 GB directory, a 2.8 percent difference attributable to bf16 and alignment, so the parameter model checks out

key_pivot: the previous round assumed both DiT and encoder must be pinned simultaneously, but that premise is unnecessary: the encoder host copy exists only as the source for the device upload, so once the encoder is resident on device the host copy can be released

two_orderings.scheme: A, naive, both pinned at once
two_orderings.verdict: does not fit, short by 22.2 GiB

two_orderings.scheme: B, encoder loaded to device once then host copy released, DiT stays pinned

verdict: scheme B passes both the pinned and the device budget with ample headroom

cost_and_benefit.one_time_scope: once per process rather than once per request

causal_chain: encoder time is about 99 percent the 63 GB transfer, compute being only 0.17 s
therefore per-call loading makes 3.15 s a hard floor and under 2 s physically impossible
therefore residency is the only route
residency needs 7.33 GiB per rank on device; the measured DiT peak is 11.64 GiB, totalling 18.97 of 32
but pinned cannot hold both host copies, 116.4 GiB against a 94.3 GiB limit
so release the encoder host copy after loading, leaving only the DiT 57.7 GiB pinned
therefore per-request encoder becomes about 0.5 s and the target is met
open_issues: whether the current code permits releasing the encoder host copy after load_to_device is unverified; today load and offload are paired calls
the lifetime of the DiT 62 GB pinned masters is not stated in R126, only that they are immutable pinned masters; if the DiT also pins per block the budget is looser
the NUMA hazard remains: 8 nodes, cross-node pinned memory lowers H2D bandwidth, and R198 did not record NUMA placement
the deployment model decides whether the 3.15 s one-off amortises, depending on whether the process is long-lived and how many requests it serves
